problem: Modular urban VLN pipelines are interpretable but lack a unified memory, while end-to-end (M)LLM agents are limited by fixed context windows and implicit spatial reasoning, so they struggle to recall experiences over long horizons in large-scale outdoor environments.
motivation: Urban VLN needs grounding of instructions in complex scenes and recall of relevant experiences over long horizons. Existing agents lack a structured, compressible and retrievable spatial memory that can be plugged into any backbone.
key_idea: A plug-in hierarchical spatial-cognition long-short memory that combines a sparse octree (voxel-level) and a semantic topology graph (landmark-level), stores them as trainable memory tokens via a reversible Transformer (lossless decoding), and adds a short-term relative-coordinate cache.
insight: The abstract reports that ablations confirm both the hierarchical map (octree + graph) and the dual memory (LTM + STM) are indispensable. Short-term retrieval prunes dynamic context, and reversible LTM tokens can be decoded losslessly when deeper history is needed. Only the abstract was available, so specific ablation numbers are not known.
method: Sparse octree: fine-grained voxel indexing of the environment for spatial memory
Semantic topology graph: high-level landmark connectivity between places
Memory tokens with reversible Transformer: trainable tokens at octree and graph nodes, losslessly decodable to reconstruct past embeddings
Long-term memory (LTM): compresses and retains historical observations at octree and graph nodes
Short-term memory (STM): caches recent multimodal entries in relative coordinates for obstacle avoidance and local planning
Retrieval: STM retrieval prunes dynamic context; LTM tokens are decoded when deeper history is needed
Backbone-agnostic plug-in: tested with a modular pipeline, a VLN model with prompt-based LLM, and a VLN model with strided-attention MLLM

setting.backbone: Three backbones: a modular pipeline, a SOTA VLN with prompt-based LLM, and a SOTA VLN with strided-attention MLLM, each augmented with Mem4Nav (specific models not given in abstract)
setting.training_data: Touchdown and Map2Seq training sets (memory tokens trainable); details not given in abstract
setting.observation: urban street-view visual observations with language instructions (details not stated in abstract)

numbers_note: abstract only; the abstract reports only aggregate gains (7-13 pp Task Completion, >10 pp nDTW, SPD reduction), no per-table values
results: On Touchdown and Map2Seq across three backbones, Mem4Nav yields 7-13 pp gains in Task Completion, sufficient SPD reduction and >10 pp nDTW improvement. Ablations show both the hierarchical map and the dual memory modules are needed. Baseline names and exact values are not available from the abstract.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so details of the setup and exact numbers are unverified
Evaluated only on street-view urban VLN benchmarks (Touchdown, Map2Seq)
